title: Light
hook: a square of late sun slides across the wall. it was behind every color this week.
tomorrow: what can you see through an empty window?

segments.voice: Yesterday, white: the color that shows every mark, and a mind called luminous, with stains that only visit. Today the week comes back, in the light.
screen: `WHITE: STAINS THAT VISIT.` → `NOW: THE WEEK, IN THE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Late afternoon, a square of sun slides slowly across a bedroom wall. It's easy to miss; it's just there. Yesterday asked what a patch of sun on a wall has to do with any of this. Here's the answer: everything this week needed it. In the dark, no flame shows and no blue or red is a color at all. So Buddhaghosa's next disc is the light itself. Sunlight or moonlight coming through a gap in a wall or a window, making a circle on the wall or floor. Or light falling through the leaves of a thick tree. Or a lamp set inside a pot, shining out through a hole in its side.
screen: `A SQUARE OF SUN ON THE WALL.` → `EVERY COLOR NEEDED IT.` → `THE NEXT DISC IS LIGHT ITSELF.`

segments.voice: The note is simple: light, light. At first the image looks like that circle on the wall. Later, the manual says, it becomes a bright, compact glow. Notice the fire's trick again: a gap in the wall does the framing, the way the hole in the mat did. And since today looks back, hold the week up to it. A flame, framed, with the sticks and smoke left outside. Wind, never seen, known by the leaves it moves. Blue, and an old argument: calm first, insight first, or both yoked together. Yellow, just the seen, before the story arrives. Red, and a fine peg to knock out an angry thought. White, and a mind called luminous. Seven objects, one thread through all of them: choose one thing, let it be plainly what it is, and rest there until the mind steadies. Light makes a fitting end to the week, because it was there the whole time, behind every other color.
screen: `LIGHT, LIGHT.` · `FIRE, WIND, BLUE, YELLOW.` · `RED, WHITE, AND NOW LIGHT.` · `ONE THING, PLAINLY WHAT IT IS.` · then, large: `LIGHT ON THE WALL.`

segments.voice: Find where light lands in your room: a window's square on the wall, a lamp's glow, sun on the floor. Rest your eyes on the brightness itself rather than the wall under it. When the mind drifts, note light, light, and come back.
Light: aloka in Pali. A circle of sun or lamplight on a wall, the disc every other color needed.
Your line: light on the wall. It was behind every color this week. That's a week of discs.

howItsDone: In Theravada meditation the light kasina uses sunlight or moonlight cast as a circle on a wall or floor, or lamplight through a hole, noted as 'light, light', as the Visuddhimagga describes; it is taken up with a teacher.

fork.setup: your little brother asks what you've been staring at all week. what's the best one-line answer?

fork.reveal: each disc is plain: fire as fire, red as red. Buddhaghosa is careful about each object, but there's no secret code. just one thing, seen plainly.
